comparison: Perfect agreement on functional assays (C5, C42-C46). Both recognize the value of Transwell, colony formation, and scratch assays showing ACVR2A knockout reduces trophoblast function. However, OpenEval flags UNCERTAIN due to potential proliferation confounding on migration/invasion assays, while peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED without noting this methodological concern.

Both address main conclusions (C58, C75) with UNCERTAIN evaluation. OpenEval cites limitations including cell line models, proliferation confounding, correlative pathway analysis, and lack of in vivo validation. Peer reviewers similarly note need for 'further validation in both in vitro and in vivo models' and 'animal models' to strengthen mechanistic conclusions.

Strong agreement on ACVR2A downregulation in PE placentas (C4, C29-C31, C33-C34). Both rate SUPPORTED with high confidence. OpenEval provides detailed statistical validation (p<0.001) and notes appropriate controls (C66, C83). Peer reviewers accept findings without challenge, with editor noting 'study is solid.'

Both support RNA-seq and GSEA findings (C6, C47-C52) showing Wnt pathway enrichment. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED noting appropriate bioinformatics methods (DESeq2, FDR<0.05). Peer Reviewer 2 highlights RNA-seq as 'valuable insights' and Reviewer 3 calls Wnt/ACVR2A cross-talk 'an important contribution.'

Agreement on TCF7/c-JUN pathway validation (C7, C53-C54). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes evidence is primarily correlative and suggests rescue experiments would strengthen causality. Peer reviewers accept pathway findings as 'valuable insights' without requesting additional mechanistic validation at this stage.

Both support western blot data showing coordinated downregulation of ACVR2A, Smad signaling, and TCF7/c-JUN components in PE tissues (C55-C57, C78). OpenEval notes appropriate acknowledgment of Smad2/3/4 not being directly assessed. Peer Reviewer 3 specifically endorses 'cross-talk between WNT and ACVR2A/SMAD2 pathways' as important.

Agreement on CRISPR/Cas9 knockout validation (C37-C41). Both rate SUPPORTED. Peer Reviewer 2 praises 'multiple experimental techniques' as 'commendable.' OpenEval provides detailed validation assessment but flags limitation of using immortalized/tumor-derived cell lines (JAR, HTR8/SVneo) that peer reviewers do not explicitly address.

Both support GWAS background and ACVR2A's genetic association with PE (C1-C3, C18-C19, C63-C64). OpenEval comprehensively covers genetic associations across populations. Peer Reviewer 3 validates 'ACVR2A is one of very few genes implicated in preeclampsia in multiple human populations' and notes study addresses knowledge gap.

OpenEval evaluates PE pathophysiology background claims (C8-C12, C59-C62, C82) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations to clinical guidelines (ACOG). No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers focused on experimental findings rather than background context.

OpenEval evaluates GWAS methodology and limitations claims (C13-C17, C63-C64) as SUPPORTED, noting they provide context for functional validation studies. Peer review R8 partially overlaps (C63-C64) but focuses on ACVR2A's specific genetic association rather than general GWAS methodology discussion.

OpenEval evaluates prior research on ACVR2A in cancer and reproduction (C32, C68-C72) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate citations and rationale for using trophoblast cell lines. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background/literature review claims.

OpenEval evaluates claims about ACVR2A's role extending to uterine/decidual mechanisms (C65, C80-C81) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers did not specifically address this contextual discussion.

OpenEval evaluates methodological details (C74, C88-C98, C104-C106) as SUPPORTED, noting standard methods with appropriate quality controls (PCR efficiency 95-100%, off-target assessment). Peer reviewers accepted methods implicitly but did not provide separate evaluation of methodological claims.

OpenEval evaluates study design and inclusion/exclusion criteria (C83, C66) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate controls minimize confounding though may limit generalizability. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing patient selection criteria.
